analysis: The closest plan connects genre, narrative, literary theory and interpretation to historical reading and related evidence from film, art, museums, society and historical research. Great Literary Works supports older and modern literary traditions. World Myth & Literature develops comparative textual analysis and reception; Life & Travel Writing adds memoir, place and identity; Film & Text treats adaptation and medium-specific analysis; the advanced interpretation course tests theories against texts in a research project. The across-borders option uses the same direct literary spine with more comparative context from rhetoric, world archaeology, environmental media and cultural circulation. Its distinctive contribution is cross-cultural and cross-media reception. The conflict option originally included two literature courses and relied too heavily on political courses. Four replacements add Introduction to Literary Studies, Great Literary Works, Film & Text and advanced literary interpretation. Textual study now precedes myth, memoir, adaptation and literary theory, where feminist, Marxist and minority perspectives supply direct study of power and representation. Histories of gender and empire, social movements, media and race, political institutions and public communication provide complementary contexts. The pairs differ by five, eight and ten courses or 37.5, 60 and 75 EC respectively. The comparative option focuses on movement and reception, and the conflict option on contested identity and cultural authority. Modern media history and sociology remain complementary, while the Republic of Letters has a distinct research and literary institutions focus. These three correspondences were moved from direct pairings to clearly separate rows. UCR optional independent research is outside the 180 EC schedule.

alignment.rationale: Both examine early modern culture. UCR focuses on Renaissance art. Utrecht focuses on literature.
Utrecht studies how literature is produced, circulated and valued and prepares students for their thesis. UCR offers related research practice across courses.
Both introduce literary genres, interpretation and close reading.
Great Literary Works includes classical and medieval texts in a broader survey. Utrecht devotes a course to those periods.
Both analyse how style and form create meaning. UCR also studies language use across genres.
Utrecht studies modern and contemporary literary history. UCR studies material media history and technologies.
Both examine mobility, identity and cultural encounters through writing.
Both examine race, identity, representation and power. UCR applies these questions to media.
Both develop critical interpretation of culture. UCR studies theories of literary meaning and reading.
Both examine environmental questions through culture. UCR emphasises visual and audiovisual media.
Utrecht focuses on contemporary debates in literary studies. UCR offers related social and cultural theory.
UCR examines the historical context of modern Europe. Utrecht studies literature from 1789 to 1914.
Both study how arguments and rhetorical choices influence audiences.
Utrecht teaches methods for literary inquiry. UCR develops related skills in qualitative research design and interpretation.
Utrecht devotes a course to utopian imagination. UCR addresses related ideas across literature and cultural studies.
Utrecht requires an individual 7.5 EC thesis after preparatory study. UCR offers optional independent research outside the scheduled courses.
Utrecht leaves 60 EC for profiling. At least 30 EC must form a coherent package.
